usage: PR quality gates for handyboy, evaluated first-match-wins from the top. This repository is authored entirely by coding agents - the harness is checked in with the code, in `.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, `.agents/hooks.json`, `.factory/settings.json`, `.entire/`, `.github/hooks/entire.json`, `.opencode/plugins/` and `.pi/extensions/` - so a gate may only ever depend on the code in front of it. Every rule set below keys off a file path, the eleven explicit gate maps all set `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` to false, and the catch-all names the `pay_down_tech_debt` profile rather than a map, which is the shape the schema documents for a baseline. A rule set with no matching_content_path leaves every gate off, so the two generated Entire hook plugins and every path whose health this repository does not own are listed first and explicitly disabled. The test suites, the native host and every first-party extension layer turn every gate on, because a repository whose code is written by agents has to be blocked by a regression in the code an agent just wrote, not by the pre-existing state of a file nobody touched.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: Generated by `entire enable --agent opencode` and overwritten on the next install - header lines 2-3 say so. No gate applies: a pull request cannot be asked to improve the code its own installer regenerates.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All seven gates off. A health finding here belongs to the Entire CLI's architecture, and a gate that fired on it would only teach a coding agent to edit a file the next `entire enable` discards.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: Generated by `entire enable --agent pi`, whose installer also substitutes `ENTIRE_CMD` at install time. Same treatment as `.opencode/plugins/**`: no gate, because the file is regenerated and never edited here.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All seven gates off; the extension is installer output.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The native host's vitest suite: 16 `*.test.ts` suites plus `harness.ts` and `setup.ts`, run by `pnpm --dir host test` in `.github/workflows/tests.yml`. Every gate is on. `host/test/secrets.test.ts` and `host/test/dispatcher.test.ts` are each touched in 4 of this repository's 21 commits, and a breaking change to the wire contract is most likely to be absorbed by a test that was quietly edited to match.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false. `hotspot_decline` is on because the suite that verifies framing, secrets and dispatch is frequently the hottest thing in an agent-authored repository, so a drop in its health should block the pull request rather than wait for a refactoring cycle.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The extension's cross-cutting suites (14 files) plus the HTML fixtures `cs` cannot read, selected by the root `vitest.config.ts`.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The 27 remaining `*.test.ts` suites under `src/`. Every gate is on: a test that grows a nested helper chain, a fourth copy of an assertion block or 649 lines of code is exactly the agent entropy the rules file measures, and a test is the one place where a wrong green result hides everything behind it.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false. The 500-line cap on the test rule sets in code-health-rules.json is what `new_code_health` enforces here.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The nine React suite files under `src/ui/`, run in jsdom.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The native messaging host: the process that holds the OpenRouter key, proxies the model stream, writes run logs and artifacts under `~/.local/share/handyboy/` and serves the dev trigger socket. Every gate is on, and this is the set where a passing gate matters most, because a defect here is a credential or a file on the user's disk.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false. The routing and proxy shapes at the top of `host/src/` are measured, not exempted: `Dispatcher.handle` sits at cc 38 across a 116-line body and `HostClient.listModels` at cc 17, and a change that makes either worse is refused.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The extension's half of the same channel: `native.ts`, `fetch.ts`, `redact.ts`. Every gate is on, mirroring `host/src/**` so that a change widening one end of the protocol has to answer to both.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The injected page world: accessibility snapshot, accessible names, humanised actions, the tab driver. Every gate is on. `scripts/check-invariants.sh` enforces the four structural stealth rules, and this gate set is the code-health half of the same boundary - a page action that stops being readable is how a humanisation detail stops applying on one path.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false. `refactoring_goals` is on so a pull request touching `src/page/actions.ts` has to name the goal in .codescene/refactor-action-plan.md that it serves or does not violate.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The LangGraph agent: both nodes, the system prompts, the toolset, the checkpointer. Every gate is on. `graph.ts` is the repository's lowest score at 3.77 and is the first target of the refactoring plan; a gate that let it decline further would leave the plan nothing to measure.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false. `supervise_goals` is on because the Leader/Follower vocabulary and the `planningInterval` control are stated requirements (R-03, R-04), not style.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The service-worker runtime: the single run slot, the tool implementations, the panel message hub. Every gate is on: `RunManager.launch` owns the one run the user is watching, and `rebindMissingTabDriver` is what stands between a closed tab and an run that silently drives the wrong one.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false. The 350-line cap on this rule set is what `new_code_health` enforces for `pageTools.ts` and `runManager.ts`.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: The userscript subsystem, which runs agent-written code inside the user's page in the `USER_SCRIPT` world. Every gate is on: a duplicated guard here is a scope escape or a lost stop flag, not a style question.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: All enabled gates on; `tag_codeowners_for_critical_code` is false.

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: Everything not named above: `src/ui/**` (the side panel and run log), `src/input/**` (the three input tiers), `src/messaging/**`, `src/storage/**`, `src/stealth/**`, `entrypoints/**`, `scripts/**`, `docs/`, `.github/`, and any directory a future change introduces. The `pay_down_tech_debt` profile is the deliberate choice for this remainder: it lets a coding agent improve a large or declining file in the same pull request that touches it without first clearing a bar that file has never met, which is the only ratchet that works on a tree with a long tail of one-off harness scripts.
rule_sets.quality_gates_doc: The `pay_down_tech_debt` profile: a change is expected to leave the touched code no worse and is allowed to pay debt down, rather than being blocked by the pre-existing state of a file that no refactoring target names. A directory that becomes hot should be promoted to an explicit rule set above with every gate on - `src/ui/**` is the obvious next candidate and is deliberately not one yet, because `cs` counts 24 lines of code in a 343-physical-line JSX component, so a file-size gate there would measure nothing.
